passage: Before the bell, Karthik leaned over Baljeet's desk. "Lend me your maths homework. Real friends let each other copy, you know." Baljeet's stomach flipped; he did want to help. "I am your friend," he said. "That's why I'll show you how to do the first sum, and then you try the rest." Karthik grumbled, but at recess they sat together and got three sums done. In art class Shreya groaned, having forgotten her colours. Baljeet slid his box across the desk without a second thought. By afternoon the box had not come back, so he asked, "Could I have my colours, please? I need the blue." She apologised and returned them at once. At lunch Ritesh sat beside him, chatty and full of jokes, and shared half a mango. Ten minutes later he asked to borrow Baljeet's new pen, then his eraser. Baljeet realised Ritesh had not spoken to him all week. "Sorry, I need them today," he said, and left it at that.

qa.q: What did Baljeet lend Shreya in art class?
qa.a: He lent her his box of colours.

qa.q: How did Baljeet's answer to Karthik differ from his reaction when Shreya needed colours, and why?
qa.a: He would not hand over his homework and offered to show Karthik the first sum so he could learn, but he freely lent Shreya his colours, a small loan, and politely asked for them back when they were late.

qa.q: What was Baljeet likely feeling when Ritesh asked for the pen and then the eraser?
qa.a: He probably felt used, because Ritesh had not spoken to him all week and was friendly only when he wanted something.

qa.q: What could Baljeet say next time a friend uses guilt to ask for answers?
qa.a: He could say he is their friend and will teach them, then offer to sit together and work it out. 🙂

grounding: Four requests from classmates show pressure, help with limits, easy generosity and being used by someone who is friendly only when they need something.
